systemMode_desc: Select medium: tensioned string with fixed ends, open-open pipe, or open-closed pipe
harmonicNumber_desc: Harmonic order formed along the string or air column
tension_desc: Elastic tension force applied to string in Newtons
linearDensity_desc: Mass per unit length of string in g/m
soundSpeed_desc: Propagation speed of sound inside the tube in m/s
damping_desc: Viscous damping and acoustic dissipation coefficient
real_length_effect: In real mode, sound waves project slightly outside the pipe opening (end correction)
real_damping_effect: In real mode, damping broadens resonance peaks and creates non-zero node minima
preset_second_harmonic_string: Second Harmonic String (2 Loops, 1 Center Node)
preset_third_harmonic_string: Third Harmonic String (3 Loops, 2 Internal Nodes)
formula_speed: Wave Speed on a Stretched String
formula_speed_desc: Wave speed is proportional to square root of tension over linear mass density
formula_stringHarmonics: Resonant Frequencies of String & Open Pipe
formula_stringHarmonics_desc: Includes all positive integer multiples of fundamental: f_n = n * f_1
formula_closedPipeHarmonics_desc: Restricted to odd integer multiples only: f_n = (2n - 1) * f_1
formula_standingEquation_desc: Complete spatial and temporal factorization from superposition of counter-propagating waves
theoryP1: When two identical harmonic waves propagate through the same medium in opposite directions with the same frequency and amplitude, their interference produces a standing wave. In a standing wave, energy does not propagate forward; instead, it alternates locally between kinetic and potential forms.
theoryP2: Locations where destructive interference is permanently complete and particle displacement remains zero at all times are called Nodes. Locations with maximum displacement amplitude are called Antinodes. The spatial distance between any two consecutive nodes or antinodes is always equal to half a wavelength (λ/2).
theoryP3: In acoustic organ pipes, an open end always acts as a displacement antinode (pressure node), while a closed end acts as a displacement node (pressure antinode). Consequently, pipes with one closed end support only odd harmonic resonances.
